about: The Marian antiphon said after low Mass in the prayers of Leo XIII, and at Compline through the long season after Pentecost. It addresses the Blessed Virgin Mary as Queen and Mother of mercy, and the banished children of Eve ask her to turn her merciful eyes toward them and, after this exile, to show them Jesus. A versicle and response follow the antiphon.

s01.translation: Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope.

s02.translation: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

s03.translation: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears.

s04.translation: Turn, then, most gracious Advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us.

s05.translation: And after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

s06.translation: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

s07.translation: Pray for us, O holy Mother of God.

s08.translation: That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

w001.function: Singular imperative of sálveo, addressed to “Regína”: literally “be well”, used as a greeting, “hail”.

w008.function: A vocative in the series begun by “Regína” (w002). The verb of the sentence is “Salve” (w001).

w014.function: Nominative in apposition to the understood subject of “clamámus” (w013).

w020.function: Nominative plural participle agreeing with the understood subject of “suspirámus” (w019).

w048.function: Imperative addressed to Mary. Its object is “Iesum” (w039).

w065.function: Passive: literally, that we may be made worthy.
